description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224, inside the project's own online inventory at :213-231, '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |' set against :223 '| CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View |' - the inverse of the prompt's mapping and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected; the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation and nothing here guesses which artefact is authoritative about intent, only about behaviour, where the source is the only oracle there is. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name: the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20. This case does not reach that WRITE, and it asserts the fact positively rather than by omission - see the confirmed-add discriminator below. WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm of READ-CCXREF-FILE at :624-629, reached through the SECOND arm of the ordered EVALUATE TRUE in VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS at :193-230. ACTIDINI arrives as eleven spaces, so the first arm's test at :196 - 'ACTIDINI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES' - is false and the account path at :197-209 is not taken; CARDNINI arrives as sixteen digits, so the second arm at :210 is the first to match. Its numeric guard at :211 passes, which is what makes this a different case from case12, where it fails; :218-219 then computes WS-CARD-NUM-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL(CARDNINI) into a PIC 9(16) receiver and :220-221 moves that receiver to XREF-CARD-NUM and back to CARDNINI, so the field is re-presented as sixteen zero-padded digits. The renormalisation is the identity for this value, and necessarily so: a COBOL class test for NUMERIC on a PIC X(16) item admits only sixteen digit characters, so any image that survives :211 already occupies the full width and nothing is left for :220-221 to pad. What :220-221 pins here is therefore that the field is echoed from the numeric receiver rather than from the raw received bytes. :222 performs READ-CCXREF-FILE, whose EXEC CICS READ at :611-619 names DATASET(WS-CCXREF-FILE) with RIDFLD(XREF-CARD-NUM) and KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-CARD-NUM) - the BASE cluster and its sixteen-character primary key, defined at app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:37 as FILE(CCXREF) with its DSNAME at :39. The EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :621-637 has exactly three arms and their source order is preserved with WHEN OTHER last (gate G30): DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :622-623 is a bare CONTINUE and is driven by case03, which arrives with a card number carried in CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED that the seeded cross-reference does hold; DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :624-629 is THIS case, and is also driven by case11 against a narrower population - what distinguishes the two is set out under CASE ALLOCATION below; and WHEN OTHER at :630-636 is the only one of the three that no parity case in this folder pins, its arm being covered instead by the unit tests over TransactionViewController.MSG_XREF_LOOKUP_FAILED, so no case here may claim it. The arm this case takes does four things and only four: MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG, MOVE 'Card Number NOT found...' TO WS-MESSAGE, MOVE -1 TO CARDNINL OF COTRN2AI, and PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN. THE ABSENT KEY, AND HOW ABSENCE WAS PROVEN: the card number is 5900000000000000. Absence was established by slicing bytes 1-16 - XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16), the first span of app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy - from ALL FIFTY rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt and confirming the value matches none of them, not by reading the head of the file. The fifty keys are each sixteen digit characters, they run from 0500024453765740 to 9805583408996588, and their leading digits span the whole range 0 to 9. One correction is recorded here rather than propagated: this fixture IS in ascending XREF-CARD-NUM order - the fifty keys were compared against their own sorted sequence and are identical to it - which is what a KSDS holds and the opposite of what this file's authoring brief asserted, so the scan covered every row on its own merits and relied on no ordering claim at all. The ordering is why the chosen value is what it is. 5900000000000000 falls strictly between the twenty-fifth key 5787351228879339 and the twenty-sixth 5975117516616077, so exactly twenty-five keys sort below it and twenty-five above: the read has to fail on EQUALITY, in the middle of the cluster, rather than by running off either end. case11 uses 9999999999999999, which sorts above the high key, so it cannot make that distinction and a translation that answered a keyed READ by comparing against the high key alone would satisfy case11 and fail here. The value is also sixteen DIGITS throughout, which matters for a reason that is easy to miss: were any character not a digit, the class test at :211 would fire first and the message would be 'Card Number must be Numeric...' with the cursor on the same field - that is case12's path, not this one, and the two are told apart only by the message text. THIS ARM EMITS NO DISPLAY: the DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD line belongs to the WHEN OTHER sibling at :631 and to its four byte-identical twins at :598, :662, :691 and :743. The NOTFND arm has no such statement, so this case declares no DISPLAY_LINE message at all, and the absence is an assertion: a translation that logged a diagnostic on a not-found - an entirely reasonable thing for a modern service to do - would be adding an emitted line the COBOL does not emit, and would fail here. NOT-FOUND IS A NORMAL OUTCOME, NOT AN EXCEPTION (gate G47): card.CardXrefRepository answers a keyed read with a discriminated outcome carrying a common.FileStatus value together with the CICS RESP and RESP2 it reports, and it never abends on the caller's behalf. That is the faithful shape because COTRN02C contains ZERO occurrences of CALL 'CEE3ABD': a missing cross-reference row is an expected result that the program turns into a screen message and a cursor position, not a failure. expectedReturnCode is therefore 0, stated rather than defaulted, and there is no thrown exception, no non-zero exit status and no abend anywhere in this expectation. Treating not-found as thrown is the likeliest way to diverge on this path, which is why gate G35 is listed below as deliberately NOT asserted rather than merely unmentioned. WHAT THE TASK NEVER REACHES, AND HOW THIS CASE PROVES IT: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 ends with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :530, which ends the CICS task from inside the paragraph. Everything after the PERFORM at :629 is consequently unreachable on this path, and two received values are chosen so that the unreachability is asserted rather than assumed. First, :223 MOVE XREF-ACCT-ID TO ACTIDINI never executes, so ACTIDINO is echoed as the eleven spaces that arrived: had the read been treated as successful, or had the move been hoisted above the RESP check, an eleven-digit account identifier would appear there instead. Second, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS at :232 onwards never runs, so its eleven blank-field arms, its three positional-shape arms and its two CSUTLDTC call sites are all bypassed - and the eleven data fields are populated here precisely so that bypassing them is observable. TRNAMTI carries '100000012.34', which is malformed for TRNAMTI PIC X(12): position 1 holds a digit rather than the sign the positional test at :340 requires, so had control reached that EVALUATE the message would read 'Amount should be in format -99999999.99' with the cursor on the amount field. It reads 'Card Number NOT found...' with the cursor on CARDNINL instead, and that substitution is the assertion. Third, CONFIRMI carries 'Y', which is the arm of the EVALUATE at :169-171 that performs ADD-TRANSACTION: a confirmed add that nevertheless writes nothing is a far stronger reading of an empty expectedWrites than an unconfirmed one, because it rules out the reading in which nothing was written merely because nothing was ever asked for. The eleven fields are echoed as typed rather than blanked, because the MOVE SPACES at :232-244 is guarded by IF ERR-FLG-ON inside the paragraph that never runs. THE SCREEN, AND WHERE EVERY WIDTH COMES FROM (practices B8 and B11): one send, because SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN is performed once and returns. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 supplies the six header items - TRNNAMEO 'CT02' from WS-TRANID at :37, PGMNAMEO 'COTRN02C' from WS-PGMNAME at :36, TITLE01O and TITLE02O verbatim from CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 in app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy at their declared PIC X(40), CURDATEO '07/19/22' as WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' as WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS. Both of the last two are readable only because the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the single instant all twenty cases in this folder use, which is what makes the run reproducible in any timezone (practice B7). :520 MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO moves a PIC X(80) field into a PIC X(78) receiver, so the rejection text appears on two channels that differ by exactly the two bytes COBOL loses on the right: WS_MESSAGE_80 carries it space-padded to 80 and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 carries it space-padded to 78. There is one message TEXT and there are two channels for it, and reporting only one of them would make the truncation at :520 unobservable. The twenty-one payload items and their widths are read from app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY: TRNNAME 4, TITLE01 40, CURDATE 8, PGMNAME 8, TITLE02 40, CURTIME 8, ACTIDIN 11, CARDNIN 16, TTYPCD 2, TCATCD 4, TRNSRC 10, TDESC 60, TRNAMT 12, TORIGDT 10, TPROCDT 10, MID 9, MNAME 30, MCITY 25, MZIP 10, CONFIRM 1 and ERRMSG 78, which sum to 396 and give the group image 12 + 21 x 7 + 396 = 555. The reason a received value reappears as an output value at all is structural: that copybook declares 01 COTRN2AO REDEFINES COTRN2AI, so the I-suffixed input items and the O-suffixed output items are two views of one span of storage. CARDNINL is not among the twenty-one. It is the symbolic map's LENGTH item, declared COMP PIC S9(4), and COBOL positions the cursor by moving -1 into it, so it is carried as the cursorField - validation and cursor metadata - and never as a payload member; the same is true of the F-suffixed flag items and the A-suffixed attribute items. ERRMSGC is an attribute item and is reported as DFHDFCOL, the default colour, because the only statement in the program that colours that field is MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :727 on the successful-add path, which this case does not take. The termination is RETURN_TRANSID rather than XCTL, and the response names its own program, mapset and map - COTRN02C, COTRN02 and COTRN2A - because :530 returns to transaction CT02 with the communication area carried forward rather than transferring control. All 22 fields of the 218-byte area are pinned and none omitted: the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in a server-side session (rule R6, gate G37), the differ compares that context in both directions, and an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked. None of them changes on this path, because no paragraph reached here writes one. THE SEED, AND WHY IT IS NOT PRE-PADDED: CCXREF is seeded from all fifty rows of the cardxref.txt fixture exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded. CVACT03Y declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID PIC 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) + FILLER PIC X(14), which is 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = 50, and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER; the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, and is the single declared owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). Seeding the whole fifty-row population rather than a slice of it is what gives the absence proof above its force. CXACAIX is not seeded as a dataset of its own: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-65 defines it as an ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY - a PATH over the same base cluster - so the alternate-index read at :578 and the base read at :611 resolve through one seeded cluster reached by two access paths, never through two tables (gate G45). This path issues only the base read, and no alternate-index read occurs. TRANSACT is declared inline because no ASCII fixture ships for that master - it is populated online, not loaded - and each of its three rows is 350 bytes summed from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy as 16+2+4+10+100+11+9+50+50+10+16+26+26+20, with the trailing FILLER PIC X(20) present and space-filled (gates G19 and G21). All three stand byte-identical on the final-state channel, which is the positive form of 'this path writes nothing', and row 0 is additionally pinned across all fourteen CVTRA05Y spans by their verbatim copybook names, with TRAN-AMT stated as its eleven-byte stored image 0000000010A rather than as a quantity, because the gate is byte parity and the zoned sign overpunch that makes it +1.01 is part of the value. Every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file (gate G46); no tenth fixture is named - the fixture set is closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII - and the code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). DEAD DECLARATIONS PRESERVED, NOT TIDIED (practice B5): WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program's 783 lines - no DATASET operand names WS-ACCTDAT-FILE and no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved - so the account master is a dead declaration and its copybook a dead include. No ACCTDAT input is declared here and no ACCTDAT row appears in any expectation, in this case or in any other in this folder: ParityHarness.seed states that the inputs member names every dataset the unit under test will read, so seeding a master the program never opens would assert a read that does not exist. The deadness is asserted as the non-event it is, and COTRN02CParityTest.DeadDeclarations proves the translation keeps both names as constants and wires no account collaborator at all. The eleven EXEC CICS verbs are RETURN(156), XCTL(508), SEND(522), RETURN(530), RECEIVE(541), READ CXACAIX(578), READ CCXREF(611), STARTBR(644), READPREV(675), ENDBR(704) and WRITE(713): four datasets are named by the program and only two are ever touched. CASE ALLOCATION AND CONTRACT, RECONCILED IN THE OPEN (practice B4): four points of this file's authoring brief did not survive contact with the folder and the harness, and each is recorded here rather than quietly absorbed. First, the brief placed the numeric guard at case11 and this NOTFND arm at case13; in the folder as built those two are the other way round, so case11 already drives this arm. It is retained here rather than replaced by a different behaviour because the two are not redundant in what they rule out: case11 seeds five cross-reference rows and a key above the high key, while this case seeds the whole fifty-row cluster and a key in its median gap, which is the only form of the assertion that rules out a keyed read implemented as a high-key comparison or as a scan of a truncated window. The positional-amount behaviour previously encoded at this ordinal is not lost: its message constant is asserted by the unit tests over TransactionViewController.MSG_AMOUNT_FORMAT and by the nested gate-G29 tests in COTRN02CParityTest, and its malformed image is retained above as this case's discriminator. Second, the brief asked for no nextProgram; the differ treats an absent scalar and a present one as distinct, and the response on this path does name its own program, mapset and map, so leaving them unpinned would leave three response fields nobody had checked. Third, the brief asked for exactly one expectedMessages entry; there is exactly one message TEXT, and it is reported on both of its declared-width channels for the reason given above, which the brief itself requires when it asks for the 80-to-78 move to be asserted. Fourth, the brief listed an ACCTDAT input; that would contradict both the harness's seeding contract and the brief's own finding that ACCTDAT is a dead declaration, so it is not declared. Nothing is renamed and no expectation is weakened by any of the four, and every binding requirement of the brief holds on this path - CONTROLLER_POJO with no HTTP, no job parameter, empty writes, return code 0, one rejection text with no DISPLAY line, the cursor on CARDNINL, ACTIDIN untouched, binding keys only, an unpadded cardxref seed, no CXACAIX table, no tenth fixture, a pinned clock and offset-summed widths. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, READ-CCXREF-FILE, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO in app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy as 16+9+11+14 = 50; app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 4+8+4+8+8+1+1+9+25+25+25+11+1+16+7+7 = 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at :72-80 as 16+16+8+1+1+16 = 58, so the passed area is 218; app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy 350; app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy 300, whose misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE would be preserved verbatim by any case that pinned it), against the symbolic-map widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COTRN02.bms, where the mapset is SIZE=(24,80), CARDNIN is LENGTH=16 at POS=(6,55) and ERRMSG is LENGTH=78 COLOR=RED at POS=(23,1), and against the real bytes of the fifty app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt rows. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers - among them a compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, the absence of any Language Environment CEE service behind CSUTLDTC, the absence of a CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks this program copies at :92-93 - and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. Because a statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one cannot, every width above was summed from a PICTURE clause and the absence of the chosen key was verified against the real fixture rather than assumed (practice B1). NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no rule forces this file into scope and no rule constrains how it is written. The absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (every literal derived and verified, no placeholder anywhere), B3 (the reference trees app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only; cardxref.txt was read fifty rows deep for the absence proof and not edited), B4 (the R-B inversion and all four allocation and contract reconciliations disclosed), B5 (dead declarations preserved, the -1 sent only to CARDNINL, ACTIDIN left untouched, the upper-case NOT and the trailing ellipsis kept, and no DISPLAY added), B7 (a pinned clock), B8 (binding keys, a named code page, explicit literals and no wildcard), B11 (every width summed from a PICTURE clause) and B12 (the provenance statement above). Rules R1, R5, R6 and R7 bind as well: R5 because the fixed-width image is the wire format and every value above is space-padded or zero-filled to its declared width, R6 because the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload, and R7 because the EVALUATE order at :621-637 is preserved with WHEN OTHER last - a restructuring this program makes easy, since it contains zero GO TO statements. GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN02C), G16 (the cardxref seed stays 36 bytes and is normalised at seed time, never pre-padded), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G19 and G21 (350-byte records whose FILLER is present and space-filled, proven by the whole-image expectation as well as by the fourteen named spans), G30 (the three RESP arms in source order with WHEN OTHER last), G37 (no server-side session state - the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload), G38 (the REENTER state, entered with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 1 so the test at :120 sends control to RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN, with the error flag set and the -1 cursor placed; this screen copies no CSSETATY and so highlights no field in either state), G45 (CXACAIX is an alternate-index finder over the CCXREF base, not a second table, and this path reads the base), G46 (binding keys, never a dataset-name literal), G47 (the CCXREF NOTFND outcome, surfaced as a common.FileStatus value rather than thrown) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object - no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path). DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because COTRN02C has none of them: G32 (zero GO TO, so no backward jump to restructure), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD', which is why the return code is 0 and no abend path exists), G39 (no pagination loop) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC). G40 does not apply either: the eight XCTL sites are elsewhere, and this path returns to its own transaction rather than transferring.
